metadata.title: Bacterial Heat-Shock Transformation of E. coli
metadata.purpose: Introduce plasmid DNA into chemically competent E. coli by a brief 42 C heat shock, recover the cells, and select transformants on antibiotic agar plates.
metadata.scope: Heat-shock (chemical) transformation of laboratory E. coli cloning strains with a supercoiled plasmid carrying a selectable antibiotic-resistance marker. Electroporation and competent-cell preparation are out of scope.
beforeYouBegin: Thaw competent cells on ice just before use; keep them cold at all times.
Pre-warm selective LB agar plates and recovery medium (SOC or LB) to 37 C.
Use a plasmid with an antibiotic-resistance marker matching the antibiotic in your plates.

tables.title: Plating scheme
tables.note: Plating two volumes gives well-separated colonies across a range of densities.

steps.criticalNotes: Keep cells on ice throughout; do not warm.

steps.action: Add 1-5 uL plasmid DNA to 20-50 uL competent cells in a chilled tube; flick gently to mix and incubate on ice.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not vortex; mix by gentle flicking to avoid damaging cells.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Add 1 - 5 μl of DNA ... incubate on ice for 20-30 mins

steps.action: Heat shock the tube at 42 C, then remove.

parameters.rawText: 42°C water bath for 30-60 secs (45 secs is usually ideal)

steps.criticalNotes: 45 s is usually ideal; do not exceed the stated range.

sourceReferences.excerpt: 42°C water bath for 30-60 secs (45 secs is usually ideal)

steps.action: Add 250-1000 uL antibiotic-free recovery medium (SOC or LB).

parameters.rawText: 250-1,000 μl LB or SOC media (without antibiotic)

steps.criticalNotes: SOC generally gives higher efficiency than LB.

steps.action: Incubate with shaking at 37 C to let cells recover and express the resistance marker.
steps.expectedResult: Recovered outgrowth culture ready to plate.

steps.action: Spread the recovery culture onto selective LB agar: 50 uL on one plate and the remainder on a second plate.

parameters.rawText: 50 μL on one plate and the rest on a second plate

steps.criticalNotes: Use a plate whose antibiotic matches the plasmid resistance marker.

sourceReferences.excerpt: 50 μL on one plate and the rest on a second plate

steps.action: Invert the plates and incubate at 37 C overnight.
steps.expectedResult: Discrete colonies visible the next day.

controls.name: Positive control (control plasmid)
controls.description: Transform a known amount of intact control plasmid to confirm competent-cell efficiency.

controls.name: Negative control (no DNA)
controls.description: Competent cells with no plasmid, plated on selective agar; should yield no colonies.

expectedOutputs: Discrete antibiotic-resistant colonies on the selective plate(s) after overnight incubation.
No (or negligible) colonies on the no-DNA negative-control plate.

troubleshooting.cause: Low competent-cell efficiency; wrong antibiotic; heat shock too long/short; no recovery
troubleshooting.solution: Use fresh high-efficiency cells; match antibiotic to marker; keep heat shock in range; allow full recovery outgrowth

troubleshooting.cause: Contaminated cells/medium or plates lacking antibiotic
troubleshooting.solution: Use sterile technique; confirm plates contain the correct antibiotic

troubleshooting.cause: Too much DNA plated or overgrowth
troubleshooting.solution: Plate less culture or dilute before plating

safety: Use sterile technique; treat live bacterial cultures and plates as biohazardous waste per institutional rules.
Handle antibiotics per their safety data sheets.
limitations: Transformation efficiency depends on competent-cell quality, plasmid size/amount, and the selection marker. The times, temperatures, and volumes here are the vendor-generic ranges from the Addgene protocol and should be tuned to the specific competent cells used (follow the cells' own datasheet where available).
